narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A high of 30°C (86°F) is expected today with mostly clear skies early and through midday, turning partly cloudy by evening. Isolated afternoon showers and thunderstorms are expected from 17:00, bringing 1 mm (0.04 in) of rain with a 55% chance. Thunder possible, peaking overnight. Winds are northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with peak gusts reaching 38 km/h (21 kt). Overnight temperatures will drop to a low of 20°C (68°F). The UV index will peak at 8.9. Air quality ground stations report an AQI of 124 at Kisumu Airport, 62 at Ochieng' Avenue, and 66 at Dunga Beach. As of 07:04, reports through 06:30: no rain; no thunder; high so far 19°C (66°F); low so far 19°C (66°F); peak sustained 4 km/h (2 kt); sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with thunderstorms likely each day. Thursday will be partly cloudy with highs of 30–31°C (86–88°F); one of four models is wet and thunder is likely. Friday remains partly cloudy at 32°C (90°F) with one of four models wet and thunder likely. Saturday will be partly cloudy with highs of 31–32°C (88–90°F), one of four models wet, and thunder likely; the call for Saturday is dry at 30%. Sunday turns mostly cloudy at 31–33°C (88–91°F) with zero of four models wet and thunder possible. Monday is partly cloudy at 31–33°C (88–91°F) with thunder likely. Tuesday is mostly cloudy at 31–33°C (88–91°F) with thunder possible. Wednesday is mostly cloudy at 29–33°C (84–91°F) with rain called at 59% and thunder possible. ECMWF holds the best rain record at Day+3 and Day+7 at 93%.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Thunderstorm activity is possible overnight, peaking at 02:00. Model PEAK CAPE values reach 2660 J/kg in Best Match, 2580 J/kg in UKMO, 1940 J/kg in ICON, 1890 J/kg in ECMWF, and 610 J/kg in GFS. Best Match, UKMO, ICON, and ECMWF exceed the thunderstorm threshold. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No official met service warning has been issued.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

On Winam Gulf, expect winds northeasterly overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 10 km/h (6 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 18 km/h (10 kt), then south-southwesterly into the evening at 13 km/h (7 kt) gusting 23 km/h (12 kt); peak gust 31 km/h (17 kt). Where thunderstorms are possible, sudden gusts well above the forecast wind present a hazard.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the northwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling with a trend of -0.6 hPa. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Basin pressure across 5 points sits between 1013.5 and 1015.8 hPa, falling by 2.0 hPa over three days.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

GFS tends not to see thunderstorms coming here, while ECMWF systematically under-forecasts peak wind and daytime highs. Today's call of 30°C (86°F) high and 38 km/h (21 kt) gusts sits near ICON and UKMO high calls and below Best Match's 44.6 km/h (24 kt) gust peak. Rain probability of 55% aligns closely with ECMWF and Best Match (57%), whereas GFS sits low at 16% despite holding the top Day+0 record. No Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) bulletin came due to a connection timeout. Data sufficiency is established with 73 checks at Day+0, 38 at Day+3, and 94 at Day+7.
